reason: Live check of a dashboard change copied two edited files into the shared main checkout, and cleanup failed to restore them for about two minutes. No skill covers live verification of a worktree change against seeded local fixtures, so the rule and the seeding recipe belong in one place.

The user-lens verification of the sign-in loop hit three traps not in the skill: the default preview config bypasses auth, a cold compile looked like a blank page, and a stale cookie kept the loop running. Each cost a re-run, so the recipe belongs with the existing live-verify steps.

Verifying a server-rendered, zone-dependent value (the dashboard "today" tile and header zone label) was faster and deterministic with curl and a Cookie header on the worktree server, with the server pinned to TZ=UTC to mirror Vercel. The browser pane also came back empty while hidden, and the cookie jar was shared with the main session and browser subagents.

This episode could not get :3100 or :3200 (peer sessions held them) and had to ship as not live-verified. The skill should say what to do in that case, so the next session does not verify on the production-pointed port.

This session re-learned four live-check facts: fixtures go stale at local midnight, the in-app browser is pinned to HKT so other organiser zones need a Playwright context, the TZ=UTC launch config must be reverted, and before/after proof works best as one grid. Add them beside the existing zone bullets.

Viewport and colour-scheme emulation carried past the check and survived reloads; the tool tells you to reset it. The 375 px overflow read is the cheap check that caught nothing wrong this time but is the one to repeat.

While a browser reviewer walked the shared :3100 dev server, the orchestrator held its edit to lib/auth.ts because hot reload would change the screens under the reviewer mid-walk. That rule is missing from the live-verify skill and will recur whenever a reviewer and an edit share the server.
Two reviewers' walks left audit rows after cleanup; the skill's zero-leftover check would read that as a failed cleanup without this note.

The episode hit a peer-held :3100 lock mid-live-check. The skill covered blocked ports but not the lock-file etiquette (message the holder, background-wait, respect the shared cookie jar), which is what the session actually did.
A closing cleanup ran an unconditional rm -f on the shared :3100 lock, which could have deleted a peer's claim. The skill already says peers hold this lock, so the release rule belongs here.

DB-02 user-lens reviewer was briefed "do NOT start or stop any server", hit a dead :3100, and handed back PARTIAL. The coordinator had to restart the server and resume the reviewer. A background watcher also timed out and exited 0 ("STILL DOWN after 240s [exited with code 0]"), which read as success.

Reviewer hand-back warned that :3100 in review mode makes signed-out staff pages open, so an auth walk run signed-out gives a false pass. The skill covers the preview config but has no probe to detect the mode before a walk.

Episode verified the /events listing fix by fetching the page with curl and comparing HTML card links and titles to the local DB (21 of 21 upcoming present, 0 of 227 past present). That recipe is reusable for any public list page and was not in the skill. It also left a dev server running without saying so in the hand-back.

A production-mode backtest surfaced three gaps not in this skill: branches gated on NODE_ENV=production never fire on a dev server; /login is magic-link only so the auth walk needs a minted session cookie; and a cron/dispatch tick writes rows for every local event, not just fixtures, so cleanup must be scoped by error signature.

A live zone walk embedded a test session cookie in a run_code script; the tool echoed the script into chat. The skill's rule covers cookies in scratch files but not this echo. Cookie reuse across ports is also a real trap in the same walk.

A user-lens reviewer reported "no response" on Send reminders now. The button had opened a confirm dialog that its scripted clicks never answered. The live-verify skill should say to handle dialogs before reporting a dead button.

The viewport emulation was cleared mid-check when the pane changed width. The tool output said so, but a click by coordinates after that would land on the wrong layout. Make the re-screenshot step explicit in the live-verify recipe.

Within one session the pane showed a stale render after parts.tsx changed on disk; measurements taken before a reload were wrong until the tab was reloaded. Live-verify skill has no reload-after-edit rule.

Dark-mode live check failed twice through the easy routes (colour-scheme emulation and a data-theme attribute); the key-plus-reload route worked. The skill covers the reset but not how to enter dark mode, so the next session repeats the dead ends.

The UX-02 backtest could not click Sign out because /account/complete never hydrated in the pane. The agent proved the server side with curl instead. That fallback, and the rule to label the click step unverified, are not in the skill yet.
A user-lens walk lost most of its call budget to coordinate clicks after Playwright MCP refused to start. Clicking by ref is the working path on the built-in browser.

The description is the trigger. This skill is the one that handles browser-lock and form-fill problems in Eventar live walks, but its description does not name them, so it would not route on those words.

The lock-holder check was missing. A walk saw several playwright-mcp processes from other sessions and correctly left them alone. That check should be a step in the skill, so the next session does not kill a peer's browser or retry in a loop.

A create form's scripted fill and keyboard venue pick both failed in a walk, and the lost step was not worth the calls. The skill should say how to fill a custom form and how to report a failed fill, so the next walk does not repeat the same loop.

The organiser walk lost a step to a guessed table name and lost roughly 30 calls and a timezone correctness check to an async venue picker. Both are live-verification traps this skill covers only in part (it has the click-by-ref rule but not the async-list or table-lookup cases).
A persona-role join guessed the staff key column and errored; the column must be read before the join, the same rule the table-name bullet already states.
A registration walk on a past-dated fixture hit a closed registration; the fix (shift the start to the future) is a repeatable step the skill does not yet name.
The walk attributed its results to a persona by reading the last Mailpit message, which is not evidence of the live session; the rule is that identity is verified, not inferred.

This episode signed the browser in through the Mailpit magic link instead of cookie injection, and it worked first time. The live-verify skill mentions Mailpit only as a source of the last-requested address, so a future walk would not know the sign-in path. The recipe includes the To-address check that stops a peer's link being used.

The walk asked for a screenshot per step, the built-in browser could not write files, and the summary had to declare the per-step screenshot requirement unmet on disk. The skill named inline screenshots but did not say how to report a shortfall, so a future walk could claim screenshots it does not have.

The skill already warns that scripted value sets can be ignored, but the episode produced a MAJOR-rated finding from exactly that artefact and had to be re-run. Give a concrete order (retype, read back, retry once) so the artefact is separated from a product bug before it is ranked.

The wake advice says tabs_select or one screenshot, but on 2026-11-03 show_pane rejected the value 'browser', tabs_select did not clear the hidden state, and a navigate followed by read_page was what returned elements. The valid show_pane values and the navigate fallback should be recorded here, along with the rule against synthetic events.

A walk's first psql query used start_at and end_at on events; the real columns are start_time and end_time, and the check-in and occurrence tables were not named. The column facts belong next to the existing agenda_blocks note so the next query does not repeat the error.
Orchestrator killed the :3100 listener by port and by pkill pattern. That is unsafe on a shared tree where peers hold :3100 via locks; the skill covers lock removal but not server stop.

The MVP walk used a React-safe setter to get past a custom dropdown that real typing could not set. The step worked, but the skill has no rule for when a synthetic setter is allowed and how it must be reported. Without one, the next walk either avoids the step or reports it as proven.

A read-back query for a disposable test user failed on its first attempt because email lives on auth.users, not public.users. This is the same column-location trap the skill already warns about for staff.user_id, and the read-back is the step that proves a live walk's writes.

On 2026-11-03 the speaker-window backtest cleanup needed child rows deleted before events, and deleted auth users via the admin API. The skill gave a cleanup order that omitted the children and did not say how to remove auth users.

Time-gated UI (check-in open/closed) was verified by moving a ZZ fixture's window with SQL and reloading. The stale-tab click proved the server refuses writes after close, which the skill does not cover. The skill's fixture-timing bullet covers only date drift, not deliberate state walks or restoring the window afterwards.

The practitioner cleanup on 2026-11-06 needed event_occurrences deleted before events, which the cleanup list omits. The orphan check was first run with stderr suppressed, so a broken query looked like an empty result. The skill should state both the table order and the fail-visibly rule.
resize_window errored because no tab was open, and the fix (navigate first) is not in the skill. Browser-step ordering is a repeatable pitfall.
The dev server on :3100 stopped during the usage-limit pause, and the walk resumed on a dead server. No skill step says to re-check the port after a pause.

Two Browser-pane pitfalls hit in the motion specimen check. A reload inside javascript_exec cut the read-back script off, and the instant drag could not test slow drag or spring-back. The skill already covers reload-after-edit and tab reset, so these extend it instead of starting a new skill.

After many hot-reload edits the console showed a class mismatch on EventCard titles. curl on the same route returned 0 for the new class while source had it, which separated a stale bundle from a code bug.

Two browser-pane traps hit in one walk: a javascript_exec after location.href fails with "tab is loading" and the shared seed tab moved to another page during the wait; and a native required field stopped the submit click before the app handler, so the error-path shake and banner check read empty and looked like a failure.

A residue count on audit_events failed on a guessed column name, and the walk reported a figure it had not measured. Reading the real columns first is the same rule line 44 states for every table; this adds the audit case that actually failed.

The walk minted a magic link for a disposable attendee and printed the link and token into chat, against this skill's existing rule. The rule covers Mailpit only; the mint path it used is not named, so the next session can repeat the leak through a different route.

A motion check tried to time a slide with requestAnimationFrame sampling and got almost no frames, so the timing claim had to be dropped. The skill has the drag caveat but not the frame-sampling one, and the next motion walk would hit the same wall.

Skill says magic links always land on /dashboard. A live backtest on :3100 landed on /account/registrations because the link's redirect_to carried next=/account/registrations. The skill must state the next-param rule so a later walk does not misread the landing page as broken.

The live backtest fetched the link by recipient search, which is safer against peer mail, but the skill only documents newest-message lookup. It also wrote the link to /tmp and then ran cat on it, which printed the token into the transcript. The skill already forbids printing the link, so the patch adds the safer lookup and the scratchpad rule.

The bar never appeared in the Browser pane because its overlay scrollbars hide classic bars. The reproduction needed injected scrollbar CSS, and the width reads were 0 until the tab was fronted. Both belong in the live-verify recipe.
A header change was reported as done with its 375/640 px checks left unrun because :3100 was down. The standing frame rule needs a home in the live-verify skill.

Mid-run the session tried to kill the :3100 dev server before `next build`, and the classifier denied it. The build then passed with the server still up. The skill should say the server does not need to stop for a build, and that a denied kill is not retried. Its trigger should also name the build case.

Dev-only overlays (Review-mode banner, Next dev badge) covered the new fixed bottom nav in the Browser pane. The agent hid them with injected CSS for the frames and disclosed it. The skill has no rule for dev overlays covering fixed UI.

A review agent sharing the Browser pane cleared the spsnap:* baselines stored in pane localStorage, so the compare script failed with a null read. Baselines need to survive a second agent on the same pane.

To render the venue-search dropdown, the pane needed canned geocoder results. The stub worked and was labelled in the caption. A future walk on any geocoded field will hit the same empty-list dead end and needs the same technique.
Two frame attempts failed or polluted the repo: one screenshot path did not exist for SendUserFile, and the retry wrote zz-after-*.png into /Users/ivan/Eventar. Scratchpad paths avoid both.
The existing probe assumed this session started the server. In r4 a peer-held server was in review mode and a lens could have walked it; the probe must run on any live server before dispatch.

The walk rendered a real EventsHome for a read-only role through a throwaway route with a query-param switch, measured the button and reason gap, sent frames, then deleted the route. The technique avoids fixtures for a role state and is reusable for any role-gated frame; it belongs with the live-verify rules.

The walk subagent's first cleanup rolled back on a participation_evidence FK. The cleanup-order line does not list that table, so the next walk repeats the rollback. Adding it to the child-first order and naming the rollback symptom.

The walk subagent kept magic-link tokens out of the transcript with a one-shot redirector. The skill's magic-link section has no such step, and the transcript-leak incident it records (2026-11-20) recurs without it. Adding the technique beside the no-print rule.

A frame of /login shipped with the Next N dev badge visible. The badge was hidden only on the event page, and navigate clears injected CSS. Adding a re-inject-after-navigate step and a read-back before the screenshot.

Before/after frames taken while the hero entrance fade was still running showed a half-faded layout, so the before frame was not settled. Rule: wait for entrance motion to finish and re-read before capturing a frame.
